newsitem.title: UK: Court showdown looms for Lloyd's Names.
newsitem.headline: Court showdown looms for Lloyd's Names.

text.p: Lloyd's of London will go to Britain's High Court on Thursday in an attempt to recoup around 200 million pounds ($333 million) still owed by Names -- the traditional backers of the 300 year old insurance market.
Test cases have been brought against three Lloyd's Names who have refused to accept a recent rescue package after a series of heavy losses in the 1980s and early 1990s.
Lloyd's is asking for summary judgement, that they have no arguable legal defence for not paying what they owe, against the Names: Geoffrey Lyons, Dennis Leighs and David Wilkinson.
The cases will not deal with any fraud allegations made by Names which, solicitor Michael Freeman said on Wednesday, remain the central plank of his clients' unwillingness to pay.
Freeman added he expected the cases to go to the Court of Appeal, whatever the outcome.
"Neither party is going to accept the first instance judgement," he said.

Around 1,800 of Lloyd's 34,000 Names still reject its compensation scheme, a vital part of the reconstruction plan after five disastrous years and losses of more than eight billion pounds ($13.3 billion) threatened the survival of the world's oldest insurance market.

The 3.2 billion pound compensation package only partially offset the massive losses suffered by Names with unlimited liability to claims, including those relating to U.S environmental and asbestosis insurance.

Losses arising from natural and industrial disasters are claimed to have been exacerbated by negligence and mismanagement within Lloyd's which left some Names unable or unwilling to meet their obligations.

Lloyd's has issued more than 880 writs against 552 Names to reclaim the debts and premiums payable to reinsure the market's liabilities with Equitas, a company set up to take on the losses run up between 1988 and 1992.

At the start of the process, Lloyd's said Names owed nearly 500 million pounds in total. In addition to the writs, it has obtained 35 default judgements for non-payment of debts, allowing it to bring bankruptcy proceedings to reclaim the amounts owed.
